clue.text: Man of the law briefly leaving car with member of family

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: leaving a car somewhere is parking it
a son is a member of a family

explanation.surface: A lawyer abandons his car and goes off with a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the last letter of PARKING to give PARKIN. C. Northcote Parkinson formulated Parkinson's Law (work expands to fill the time available).
explanation.definitionFit: Parkinson gave his name to a famous law, so he is literally a man of that law.

clue.text: Smarten quiet place to skate

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a rink is where people skate

explanation.surface: A quiet ice rink gets spruced up.
explanation.definitionFit: To prink is to dress up or tidy oneself fussily.

clue.text: Call for servant to be familiar

definitions.meaning: to summon a servant one rings a bell
something that rings a bell seems familiar

explanation.definitionFit: Ringing a bell summons a servant, and an idea that rings a bell sounds familiar.

clue.text: Demanding son is purposefully occupied outside

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: someone intent on something is purposefully occupied with it

explanation.surface: A pushy son is busy outdoors with a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts INTENT around SIS: IN-SIS-TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent means demanding firmly and repeatedly.

clue.text: One threatening to cleave skull at parting of hair

definitions.text: One threatening to cleave skull at parting of hair

parts.words: One threatening to cleave skull at parting of hair
parts.note: a blade hung over a courtier's head by a single strand, ready to split his skull should the strand part

explanation.walkthrough: 'parting of hair' looks like a hairstyle parting, but means the hair snapping. Damocles sat under a blade hung by one horsehair.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary blade hung by a single hair over Damocles's head symbolises ever-present peril.

clue.text: Never anti-social work?

indicators.note: work suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asks if compulsory military duty was never antisocial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges NEVERANTISOCIAL. National Service was compulsory military service in Britain until 1960, work done for the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory service for the nation is work that is, in a sense, social rather than antisocial.

clue.text: Smear book, giving "brief description of it

parts.note: to smear is to blur

explanation.surface: Someone rubbishes a book while summarising it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'it' being the book: a blurb sits on a book's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's short promotional summary printed on a book's jacket is exactly this.

clue.text: In radar image, mark barrage balloon

indicators.note: In means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a blip is a spot on a radar screen
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: A barrage balloon appears as a mark on the radar screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, the type used as a barrage balloon in wartime.

clue.text: Learned body abroad formally decide to cancel first degree

indicators.note: cancel first means the opening letter is struck out

parts.note: to rule is to decide formally, as a judge does
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A foreign academy formally votes to scrap its first degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: RULE loses its first letter to give ULE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulema are the body of Muslim scholars learned in Islamic law, found in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Bishop, say, knowing noted geisha?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to say is to utter
fly is slang for shrewd or knowing

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows he is well acquainted with a famous Japanese hostess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop, say' looks like an example phrase, but Bishop and say are separate pieces. Madame Butterfly is Puccini's opera heroine, a geisha.
explanation.definitionFit: Cio-Cio-San, called Butterfly, is the geisha heroine of Puccini's opera Madama Butterfly.

clue.text: As playwright, I love to replace : head of cultural body

indicators.note: the new letter is to stand in for the first letter of the following word

parts.note: UNESCO is the UN's educational, scientific and cultural organisation
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A dramatist says he would love to take over as boss of a cultural organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As playwright' reads as a self-description, but As is a link. Eugène Ionesco was a Romanian-French absurdist dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionesco wrote The Bald Soprano and Rhinoceros, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Be at anchor, protected by explosive weapon

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded by it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: TNT is a well-known explosive
a ship at anchor is said to ride

explanation.surface: A moored vessel is guarded by an explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'ride at anchor' is the nautical idiom, so RIDE alone means be at anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, a weapon in myth and gladiatorial combat.

clue.text: Silent film star's lost on poet

indicators.note: lost tells us some letters drop out of the word before

parts.note: Buster Keaton was a silent film comedian; the 's supplies an S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silent film star's appeal is wasted on a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ON from KEATON'S to leave the Romantic poet John Keats.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, author of the great odes.

clue.text: Adopt role in play — it keeps name before the public

definitions.text: it keeps name before the public

indicators.note: the letters are put into play, that is, moved about freely

explanation.surface: An actor takes on a part in a stage play that keeps his name in the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges ADOPTROLE. The definition is a cryptic description: a plate on a door shows the occupant's name to callers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate on a front door displays the resident's name to anyone passing.

clue.text: Diver pulling maritime hazard back to middle of sea

indicators.note: back tells us to read the hazard word from end to start

parts.note: a berg (iceberg) is a danger to ships

indicators.note: the central letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A deep-sea diver tows an iceberg back into the open ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BERG into GREB; the middle of 'sea' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a water bird that dives for its food.

clue.text: Impatient businessmen that can't wait for deliveries?

definitions.meaning: people who would rather go and fetch things than wait for them to arrive

explanation.definitionFit: Go-getters are ambitious go-ahead people; read literally, they go and get things rather than await delivery.

clue.text: Employees joining plant in Arizona community

parts.note: a flag is an iris, a plant of wet ground
the employees of a firm are its staff

explanation.surface: Workers sign on at a plant in an Arizona town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks industrial but means the flag iris. Flagstaff is a city in northern Arizona.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstaff is a city in Arizona, near the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: Gentle bell sound Debussy originally introduced in piano part

parts.note: gentle means soft

indicators.note: introduced in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a peal is the sound of bells

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Soft bell tones in Debussy were first brought into a piano piece.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the first letter of Debussy, goes inside PEAL to give PEDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft pedal is the left pedal of a piano, which quietens the tone.

clue.text: Stars also taking' more trouble with hairstyle

parts.note: also means and

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of the word are disturbed

parts.note: a DA (duck's arse) is a 1950s greased-back hairstyle

explanation.surface: Film stars go to more trouble with their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges MORE as ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a group of stars, as well as a galaxy.

clue.text: Show of charity moved Saint Paul's audience

parts.note: a gala is a festive show, often held for charity

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the next word are shifted around

explanation.surface: A charity performance stirs a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges SAINT as TIANS. 'Saint Paul's' looks like one unit, but Saint is fodder and Paul's begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Epistle to the Galatians was addressed to the Christians of Galatia.

clue.text: Crazy about food — is it fine to throw in a little yoghurt?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
to throw in is to add

indicators.note: a little of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A fussy eater asks whether a spoonful of yoghurt may be stirred into the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddy person is fussy, with odd fixed whims about what they eat.

clue.text: One running, very, slowly, we hear, going to flag

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a trickler is something that runs out very slowly

explanation.surface: A slow jogger says they are about to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like the verb to tire, but it is the definition, a three-coloured banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a flag of three bands of colour, such as the French national flag.

clue.text: Endless boring work I led bloody stuff

indicators.note: led means the I comes in front of the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a chore is a boring task

explanation.surface: Someone complains of led a dreary job amid gore.
explanation.walkthrough: CHORE without its last letter gives CHOR, which I leads. Ichor is the fluid said to flow in the gods' veins instead of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is the ethereal fluid in Greek gods' veins, their equivalent of blood.

clue.text: Acknowledged one has to keep wife and daughter

indicators.note: has to keep means the word holds another piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits that they must support a wife and daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to admit or acknowledge it, as in owning up.

clue.text: Academic circle held demonstration

indicators.note: held means one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A university group staged a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstration' suggests a protest march, but it means evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof is a demonstration that something is true.

clue.text: Suffering a lot over missing hearing given time inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other
over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: someone deaf is missing their hearing

explanation.surface: Someone who is suffering badly after going deaf is given time inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DEAF into FAED; T goes inside to make FA-T-ED. 'a lot' means one's lot, destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fated means undergoing a destiny, one's allotted lot in life.

clue.text: In Macbeth, an old porter uses it

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The drunken porter in Macbeth makes use of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's porter scene is famous for drink; the definition says porter, the dark beer, contains this alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the alcohol in beers such as porter.

clue.text: Thrash at which Independent was present, supplying spirit

indicators.note: at which places the abbreviation at the front of the thrashing word

parts.note: to thrash is to welt, to beat leaving weals

explanation.surface: A reporter from The Independent newspaper was there to see a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Independent looks like the newspaper but is just IND, independent.
explanation.definitionFit: To indwell is to be present within, as a spirit dwelling in a person.

clue.text: Second jazz instrument

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A second jazz instrument joins the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is a Stradivarius, a violin made by Antonio Stradivari.

clue.text: Announce lift out of bounds for percussionists

indicators.note: to announce is to say out loud, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: to lift is to steal, and out of bounds is banned

explanation.surface: Say that lifting is prohibited for the drummers.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel band is a group of musicians playing steel pans, which are percussion instruments.
